For every brutally dense motherfucker who thinks vr tech is about motion control:

It's for stereoscopic vision, field of vision, sense of scale, and pov tracking:

Stereoscopic vision: Depth perception, real depth perception. Lack of this is the reason most racing games have a third person mode; It's hard as fuck to properly gauge a turn when you can't accurately tell the turn from the straight. It makes judging any distance easier. It's also cool as fuck.

Field of vision: On any display short of triple monitor, your vision is basically "looking down a tube". VR headsets give you a much wider field of vision, giving you true peripheral vision, you can now glance to your left and right, catch things happening to the sides, etc.

Sense of scale: This is a big one, probably the biggest. You think you know how big something is displayed on your screen? Nope, not even close. Seeing a gameplay video of Elite dangerous on a normal screen makes the cockpits look small and cramped. Elite dangerous in VR however shows you your cockpit is the size of a small room! No conventional screen will ever give you sense of scale.

POV tracking: This ties into everything above; Even with a head tracking device like TrackIR, You still have to have your head pointed at the screen, You can't really turn around and check your six, or lean over and around something for a better view, or get a shot of something in the corner of your eye (unless you have triple monitor).
